column3: “The sleep of the king fled” is rendered “the king could not sleep,” and “said” as “gave an order.” “The book of the reminders, the words of the days” is rendered “the book of records, the chronicles.”
“Told on” is rendered “reported concerning,” and “from the guards of the threshold” as “who were doorkeepers.”
“Greatness” is rendered “dignity,” and “young men” as “servants who attended him.”
“Said in his heart” is rendered “said to himself,” and “do honor excess more than me” as “desire to honor more than me.”
“Clothing of royalty” is rendered “a royal robe,” and “a head-dress of royalty” as “a royal crown.” The Hebrew may mean the crown is placed on the horse's head, as NASB has it.
“On the hand of” is rendered “handed over to,” and “make him ride” as “lead him on horseback.” “The open place of the city” is rendered “the city square.”
“Make fall a word” is rendered “fall short in anything.”
“Make him ride” is rendered “led him on horseback.”
“Covered of head” is rendered “with his head covered.”
“Offspring of the Jews” is rendered “of Jewish origin”; “prevail to him” is rendered “overcome him.”
“Made haste to bring” is rendered “hastily brought.”
